note: PET occupancy is calibration data for the adopted binding stage (J) and a held-out test only for the bottom-up stage A.

PK structure two-compartment (fp fixed at 0.95); every training row, including the 24 h concentrations (C24) and the once-daily steady-state rows, is plotted against its prediction. Fit notes: pk_fit_notes.txt.

Black: Rabiner 2011 single-dose occupancy at 4 h. Lines: model occupancy for the same regimen and scan time; hollow markers: the row-level predictions scored in script 03. Stage A (bottom-up) fits no PET row and is the only genuine held-out prediction; stage A2 is calibrated on these Rabiner rows; stage J is calibrated on all PET rows, so its agreement is a calibration, not a validation.

Black circles: Lee 1988, 50 mg single dose, percent blockade normalised to that study's own 1 h scan (curves on the same estimand, 100 x RO(t) / RO(1 h)). Black triangle: Weerts 2008, absolute occupancy (mean +/- SD) after 4 once-daily 50 mg doses, at an ASSUMED 24 h after the last dose (scan interval not reported; pet_weerts_scan_time_sensitivity.csv); hollow triangles: each stage's prediction for that row; hollow circles: the scored Lee predictions. A normalised curve can exceed 100%: under a slow association rate, occupancy is still rising at the 1 h reference scan, so later occupancy exceeds the reference.
Posterior predictions use the adopted stage-J exposure cache; 300 posterior draws per hypothesis.

Rows ordered by trial, then follow-up day, then hypothesis. Black: observed LDN minus placebo difference in change from baseline with its 95% CI (observed +/- 1.96 x the SE used for scoring; for INNOVA the unadjusted difference of the arm changes, SE borrowed from the adjusted 95% CI). Wide pale bar: posterior predictive 90% interval for the OBSERVED difference (model draws plus observation error), against which inside90 is judged; thin bar: 90% interval of the TRUE difference (model draws only); point: predictive median. Primary endpoints: FINAL day 84, INNOVA day 90; other INNOVA days are secondary and correlated.
Cytokines without a curated half-life have no prediction and are not plotted (listed in Table 3).

Violins: simulated LDN - placebo differences at each trial's actual design (omega as calibrated). Solid line: observed (unadjusted) difference; dashed: INNOVA's LMM-adjusted level difference (sensitivity estimand). p: two-sided posterior predictive p-value of the observed difference (2 x the smaller tail).

Line: stage-J mean steady-state occupancy over one dosing interval (certified steady state). Error bars at 1.5, 4.5 and 6 mg: 95% Laplace bands for the binding scales alone and jointly with independent PK draws (the joint band ignores the PK-binding correlation, so it is approximate, not a strict superset of the binding-only band). Open circles: Rabiner 2011 occupancy at 2 and 5 mg, single doses scanned at 4 h; they are reference points, not steady-state means.

Dashed line: the adopted stage's point value. Probability bands (blue) and structural sensitivities (orange) are reported side by side; the structural rows are refits, not probability statements. Stages A2 and A bound the binding assumption from outside. Shifts from the point value: terminal-phase PK -10.3 pp; koff_BN base = koff_NTX +6.1 pp (and a worse PET fit, weighted SSE 27.2 against 11.9); fp 0.90-0.99 -0.1 to +0.1 pp; keq 0.5-8 per h -11.4 to +9.1 pp.

Rejection rates of a one-sided 5% test whose critical value comes from H0 replicates (independent seed). A: hypotheses whose net effect at day 84, evaluated at the posterior-median parameters, exceeds the threshold (effect_eligibility.csv); their rate averages power over the posterior, i.e. assurance. B: H0 as the type-I-error check; solid with model-structure uncertainty, dotted sampling variability only (the two variants differ by at most 0.003 anywhere). Hypotheses below the threshold have no curve.

First-order indices by the Sobol 2007 estimator and total indices by Jansen's estimator, both from the same model runs (Saltelli et al. 2010). Jansen's first-order estimate (S1_jansen) is high-variance on these heavy-tailed outputs (its variance term comes from one sample) and is not shown. Parameters vary uniformly over their marginal 95% posterior intervals; only hypotheses whose net effect exceeds the threshold are analysed. Each index was computed with two seeds; x marks an index whose two estimates differ by more than the larger bootstrap CI half-width (7 of 36 plotted indices; sobol_seed_agreement.csv).

SD sensitivity: variability recalibrated to the Younger 2013 SDs quoted by Bested et al. 2023 (FIQ pain reduction, sample-size section; 14.6 placebo, 12.5 LDN). It is a consistency check, not a candidate calibration; its responder rates are compared with the primary calibration's in tableS_responder_calibrations.csv.
